methodology.split: Chronological development60%/validation20%/test20% by UTC-hour count; no fitting or fine-tuning
methodology.origins: Deterministically evenly spaced from a 24-hour origin grid within each split; sampled subset, no selection by errors
methodology.forecast: Direct model calls with prediction_length 6, 12, and 24 for each target/origin. Held-out windows are nested across horizons, so horizon results are dependent
methodology.context: Only observations timestamp <= origin; no future covariates; gaps remain explicit and incomplete windows are skipped
methodology.intervals: Chronos raw q0.1/q0.9, nominal80%, uncalibrated. Baseline test bounds from validation-only pooled hourly residual q0.1/q0.9
methodology.point_forecast: q0.5 median (same point estimate used by deployed service)
methodology.rainfall: Precipitation mm per previous hourly interval, used as rainfall proxy in Malaysia; sum-of-medians is not a total quantile
methodology.reference: Open-Meteo historical reanalysis, not independent station ground truth or as-of operational observations
methodology.leakage: Application input chronology enforced. Pretraining corpus overlap and training cutoff unknown; absence of pretrained-model leakage cannot be guaranteed

runtime.memory_note: Whole evaluation process high-water RSS including imports/model/data, not model-only allocation or container memory

limitations: Small retrospective sample; no claim of operational forecast skill or official meteorological forecast
Reanalysis was acquired after evaluation dates and may include revisions/assimilation unavailable at forecast origin
Sparse rainfall and a short sample make interval coverage and wet-hour scores unstable
Raw quantiles are not calibrated rainfall-event probabilities; exposure rules do not predict telecom outages
If a baseline wins, retain the integration and enlarge blind evaluation before choosing a deployment forecast method
